value.body: Regular medical officer posts in state-run Ayush hospitals and dispensaries for Ayurveda, Homoeopathy, Siddha or Unani. States recruit through their Public Service Commissions or health recruitment boards, such as Tamil Nadu's Medical Services Recruitment Board. The work covers outpatient care, ward duty, public-health programmes and reporting.

items.label: Qualification
items.note: Posts are specific to one system of medicine

items.label: Registration
items.value: State Ayush board/council or the national register
items.note: Kept under NCISM (Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani) or NCH (Homoeopathy)

items.label: Recruiting body
items.value: State PSC or state health recruitment board

items.label: Registered AYUSH practitioners
items.note: All six systems (Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, Homoeopathy, Sowa-Rigpa and others); not all are in government service
items.source: Ministry of Health / Ministry of Ayush, reply in Parliament (as reported)

items.label: BAMS students enrolled
items.note: All years of the BAMS programme; institutions that reported to AISHE

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A recognised degree in the matching system, a completed internship and current registration. Apply when your state's PSC or health recruitment board notifies posts; selection is by written exam, sometimes with an interview, and a few states select on merit. Domicile, local-language and age rules usually apply.

value.title: At a glance
items: Vacancies come irregularly and their number differs widely from state to state.
A BHMS graduate applies for Homoeopathy posts, a BAMS graduate for Ayurveda posts, and so on.
Contract medical officer posts under the National Ayush Mission or NHM exist alongside regular posts and have different terms.
Central government Ayush posts are recruited separately from state posts.
